newsitem.title: INDIA: India will remove hurdles on investment - Deve Gowda.
newsitem.headline: India will remove hurdles on investment - Deve Gowda.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said on Monday the government will do everything to remove hurdles that block foreign investment and denied there was any dilly-dallying in decision-making.
"Decision-making is my first hobby," Deve Gowda told a large gathering of foreign and local industrialists. "We'll create a climate for investors so that no one is disappointed."
Earlier some speakers at the meeting spoke of bureaucratic delays and red tape in approving foreign investment projects.
The prime minister, inaugurating a two-day Global Investors' Convention, did not give any details of how the government planned to cut through the red tape and speed up approvals.
He said the 13-party coalition government that he headed had decentralised decision-making, by giving more powers to states.
The western Maharashtra government signed a $1 billion deal with P&O Australia Pvt Ltd on Monday to develop a port, with the federal government having little say in the deal.
Deve Gowda said plans were afoot to open up oil exploration.
"In oil exploration I want to go in big way for privatisation," he said.
He said India was a vast country with huge natural resources.
"(The north-eastern) Arunachal Pradesh has potential to general 30,000 megawatts of hydel power... Kashmir has potential for 15,000 megawatts," he said.
The convention is being attended by 900 delegates from 25 countries.
